newsitem.title: TURKEY: OLYMPICS-TURK PRESIDENT HOPES ISTANBUL WILL TRY AGAIN.
newsitem.headline: OLYMPICS-TURK PRESIDENT HOPES ISTANBUL WILL TRY AGAIN.

text.p: Turkey's President Suleyman Demirel said on Friday he was saddened Istanbul did not make the shortlist of five candidates to host the 2004 Olympics and hoped it would still try to host future games.
"President Suleyman Demirel said he was saddened Istanbul was not selected among the five candidates," a statement from his office said.
"He wanted the work (of the National Olympic Committee) not to go to waste and to continue with the same eagerness for the 2008 Olympics," it said.
Istanbul was one of six candidates to be rejected alongside Lille, Rio de Janeiro, San Juan, Seville and St Petersburg.
After the decision was announced in Lausanne, the Istanbul delegation hit out at what it suggested might be any anti-Moslem bias within the IOC.
"Never in the history of the Olympics has a Moslem country got to stage the Games," the delegation's Erman Tuncer said.
"Are we seeing here the emergence of a Christian crusaders' mentality? The two-billion-strong Moslem community of the world is being excluded from the Olympics."
